synopsis: Recall (true positive rate) measures the share of real objects found, precision measures the share of reports that are real, and F1 combines them using their harmonic mean; both precision and recall matter, as a 2026 labeler achieved recall of 0.88–0.98 but precision of only 0.52 in crowded indoor scenes [f12841, f5382]. The recommended baseline measures detection per independent encounter by object class, distance, bearing and condition, reports curves or bins rather than a fleet average, and includes real-data confidence intervals and audited-label precision and recall [f14339, f11102, f5422]. Demonstrating at least 95% or 99% detection with 95% confidence requires respectively 59 or 299 consecutive successful encounters per stratum, but no acceptance value for detection probability or miss rate was found [f5202, f5203, f2620]. Replay establishes detection, false-alarm rates and warning timing only for recorded configurations and situations; probability-based sampling supports unbiased estimates for the assumed scenario distribution, while poor field telemetry leaves aggregate real-world weighting uncertain [f13444, f6830, f7423]. Detector-threshold tuning using ROC, DET or precision-recall operating points is recommended, but specific off-road evidence was not identified, and detection-only validation can overlook nuisance braking that prompts operators to disable the system [f6980, f7306, f1986]. The 2022 off-road lidar de-dusting result of F1 = 97.55% measures filter performance on its own dataset, not sensor-model fidelity, while synthetic coverage can make mAP misleading despite real–simulation differences [f10563, f7832, f12842].
